newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan hopes to buy more U.S. missiles - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan hopes to buy more U.S. missiles - paper.

text.p: Taiwan is hoping to buy advanced medium-range air-to-air and air-to-ground missiles from the United States to bolster the island's air defence, the United Daily News reported on Sunday.
The missiles would be carried by the 150 F-16 fighter planes Taipei already has ordered from Washington, the mass-circulation newspaper said.
It did not say how many missiles Taiwan wants to buy.
The United States would decide whether to approve the sale in early 1997, the newspaper said.
Taiwan's defence ministry officials were not available for confirmation.

Any U.S. weapons sale to Taiwan is a sensitive issue because China, which sees Taiwan as a renegade province, condemns foreign bolstering of Taipei's military as an act that encourages unrest within Beijing's sphere of sovereignty.
China and Taiwan split after a civil war in 1949 but Beijing vows to bring the island under its rule eventually and threatens to attack if Taipei tries to pursue independence.
Despite switching diplomatic recognition to Beijing from Taipei in 1979, Washington reserves the right to provide Taiwan with defensive weapons.
In August the United States approved sale to Taiwan 1,299 Stinger missiles, launchers and other equipment despite China's protest.
Earlier, in December, the U.S. Army announced it had awarded a US$63 million contract to Boeing Defence and Space Group, Missiles and Space Division, to produce 75 Avenger fire units for Taiwan.
Washington also has approved a deal to sell Taipei 150 F-16 fighters.
